parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  WHAT IS ARGUMENTATIVE WRITING?
content: Argumentative writing tries to CONVINCE the reader to agree with your OPINION.
- What you believe and will prove
- Example: "Homework should be banned in primary schools."
- Example: "Studies show 70% of students feel stressed about homework."
- Example: "Some people say homework helps students practice."
- Why the other side is wrong
- Example: "However, students can practice in class instead."
Good argumentative writing is LOGICAL, ORGANIZED, and PERSUASIVE!

listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text:
What is Argumentative Writing?
Argumentative writing tries to CONVINCE the reader to agree with your OPINION.
KEY ELEMENTS:
1. CLAIM (Thesis)
- Your main argument
- What you believe and will prove
- Example: "Homework should be banned in primary schools."
2. REASONS
- WHY you believe your claim
- At least 3 strong reasons
- Example: "Homework causes stress."
3. EVIDENCE
- FACTS that support your reasons
- Statistics, examples, expert opinions
- Example: "Studies show 70% of students feel stressed about homework."
4. COUNTERARGUMENT
- The OTHER SIDE's argument
- Show you understand different views
- Example: "Some people say homework helps students practice."
5. REBUTTAL
- Why the other side is wrong
- Example: "However, students can practice in class instead."
Good argumentative writing is LOGICAL, ORGANIZED, and PERSUASIVE!
dictation: Argumentative writing tries to CONVINCE the reader to agree with your OPINION.
